entries.name: Playing through a noisy channel (and knowing it)
entries.abstract: We study combinatorial games played through a noisy channel, where the move chosen by a player may differ from the move that is effectively executed. The key feature of this setting is that any received legal move is accepted as the move played, regardless of the player's original intention, while illegal moves trigger retransmission. Both players know the error mechanism and strategically choose their transmitted moves to maximize their winning probabilities. This interaction between strategic choice and imperfect execution gives rise to a rich class of games whose behavior can differ substantially from that of the underlying combinatorial game. We develop a general framework based on move error functions and establish structural results concerning winning probabilities, optimal moves, and conditions for fair chance games. We then investigate in detail one-pile Nim with independent binary transmission errors. Despite its apparent simplicity, this example exhibits unexpectedly intricate behavior. We determine optimal strategies and winning probabilities in the low-error regime and uncover a substantially richer structure in the high-error regime, including changes in optimal play and nontrivial limiting behavior.

entries.name: Tightness for branching random walk in a space-inhomogeneous random environment
entries.abstract: We consider the maximum $M_t$ of branching random walk in a space-inhomogeneous random environment on $\mathbb{Z}$. In this model the branching rate while at some location $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ is randomized in an i.i.d. manner. We prove that there is a centering $\widetilde{m}_t$ depending only on the environment such that $(M_t-\widetilde{m}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is tight in an annealed sense.

entries.name: Ergodic theorems for set maps under weak forms of additivity
entries.abstract: We investigate various relaxations of additivity for set maps into Banach spaces in the context of representations of amenable groups. Specifically, we establish conditions under which asymptotically additive and almost additive set maps are equivalent. For Banach lattices, we further show that these notions are related to a third weak form of additivity adapted to the order structure of the space. By utilizing these equivalences and reducing non-additive settings to the additive one by finding suitable additive realizations, we derive new non-additive ergodic theorems for amenable group representations into Banach spaces and streamline proofs of existing results in certain cases.

entries.name: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof
entries.abstract: We show that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation Property. This question has been open for many years. Three proof attempts were published, but later criticized in the literature or retracted. Our proof is based on the main ideas from Borzechowski (1988, master thesis). We define a cyclic tableau system for PDL with a loading mechanism to recognize successful repeats. For this system, we show soundness and completeness via a game. To show interpolation, we modify Maehara's method to work for tableaux with repeats: we first define pre-interpolants at each node, and then use a quasi-tableau to define interpolants for clusters (strongly connected components). In different terms, our method solves the fixpoint equations that characterize the desired interpolants, and the method ensures that the solutions to these equations can be expressed within PDL. The proof is constructive and we show how to compute interpolants. We make available a Haskell implementation of the proof system that provides interpolants, and a formal verification of our proof in the interactive theorem prover Lean. Lastly, we discuss several questions for future work.

entries.name: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics
entries.abstract: The capabilities of generative AI in mathematics education are rapidly evolving, posing significant challenges for research to keep pace. Research syntheses remain scarce and risk being outdated by the time of publication. We present a Living Meta-Analysis (LIMA) on the effects of generative AI-based interventions on mathematics learning. We update the literature base every two months and apply a cumulative Bayesian multilevel meta-regression model. This paper reports results from the sixth version, including 37 studies, five of which were added since the fifth version. Results indicate a robust overall positive effect (g = 0.52, 95% CrI [0.32, 0.72]) and no evidence in favor of publication bias. Moderator analyses provided strong evidence for including integration mode, intervention dose, and grouping. Estimated effects were larger when generative AI supplemented teacher instruction, with greater intervention dose, and in group, teacher-led, or tutoring settings. For the remaining moderators, evidence was moderate or inconclusive.

entries.name: Symmetry of some noncommutative sphere algebras
entries.abstract: Two known $q$-deformed (or `quantum') $7$-spheres, both denoted $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ in the literature, may be distinguished by the presence or absence of symmetry under $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$. The quaternionic version of $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ has been shown by Brain and Landi to support such a symmetry. Here we show that this is not the case for the older $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ introduced by Vaksman and Soibelman: and as a consequence, these quantum $7$-spheres are not isomorphic.

entries.name: Construction of two-bubble solutions for the energy-critical Hartree equation
entries.abstract: We construct a pure two-bubble solution for the focusing, energy-critical Hartree equation in space dimension $N \geq 7$. The constructed solution is spherically symmetric, global in (at least) the negative time direction and asymptotically behaves as a superposition of two ground states (or bubbles) both centered at the origin, with the ratio of their length scales converging to $0$ and the phases of the two bubbles form the right angle. The main arguments are the modulation analysis, the bootstrap argument and the topological argument. The main novelty with respect to existing constructions of pure two-bubble solutions is the nonlocal interaction, which is more complex to analyze.

entries.name: Borel exceptional values in several complex variables and their applications to shared values of shifts and difference operators
entries.abstract: In this paper, we investigate shared value problems for shifts and higher-order difference operators of meromorphic and entire functions in several complex variables. Using Nevanlinna theory in $\mathbb{C}^n$, we obtain new uniqueness theorems when functions share values counting or ignoring multiplicities, extending several classical one-variable results to higher dimensions. A key contribution of this work appears in Section 2, where we establish fundamental results on Borel exceptional values in several complex variables. These propositions provide the main tools for proving our principal theorems. As applications, we derive conditions ensuring that a transcendental entire function satisfies $Δ_c^{k} \equiv d\hspace{.05cc} f$ and we study meromorphic solutions of certain partial differential-difference equations, obtaining growth estimates and structural descriptions of entire solutions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of such shared value problems for higher-order difference operators in several complex variables.

entries.name: Local square mean in the hyperbolic circle problem and sums of Salié sums
entries.abstract: Let $Γ\subseteq \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a finite volume Fuchsian group. The hyperbolic circle problem is the estimation of the number of elements of the $Γ$-orbit of $z$ in a hyperbolic circle around $w$ of radius $R$, where $z$ and $w$ are given points of the upper half plane and $R$ is a large number. An estimate with error term $e^{\frac 23R}$ is known. Recently, taking $z=w$ and considering $Γ= \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, we have shown the estimate $e^{\left(\frac 9{14}+ε\right)R}$ for the local $L^2$-norm of the error term, which is better than the pointwise bound. Here we improve the exponent $\frac 9{14}$, conditionally on a twisted Linnik-Selberg-type conjecture for sums of Salié sums.

entries.name: Near-Optimal Learning of Gaussian Sobolev Operators
entries.abstract: A key question in operator learning is how to design surrogate operators with provable approximation guarantees in reasonable computational time. Whereas holomorphic operators can be approximated efficiently, i.e., with at least algebraic convergence in the number of training samples, learning finitely regular operators is known to be less efficient. The reason is an intrinsic curse of sample complexity, which allows only subalgebraic convergence rates. This fact makes it all the more important to develop algorithms which provably achieve these rates. In this work, we present a fully data-driven algorithm, termed Hermite-PCA approximation, for learning Gaussian Sobolev operators with near-optimal sample complexity. It employs principal component analysis and weighted least-squares methods and is therefore computationally efficient. Moreover, it is spectral, in the sense that it achieves faster (and near-optimal) convergence as the Sobolev regularity increases. We provide a full error analysis of this algorithm along with numerical experiments that match our theoretical results and empirically confirm the efficacy of Hermite-PCA approximation for learning Sobolev operators.

entries.name: Adaptive Volumetric Parameterization of Simply Connected 3-Manifolds with Applications
entries.abstract: Volumetric parameterization, the process of mapping a 3-manifold onto a simplified volumetric domain, is important for many tasks in computer graphics and imaging science. However, most prior volumetric parameterization approaches have only utilized standardized domains such as a solid ball regardless of the overall shape of the given 3-manifolds, which introduces significant geometric distortion and affects the subsequent shape processing and analysis tasks. To overcome this issue, in this work we propose a novel volumetric parameterization framework for simply connected 3-manifolds. Specifically, the proposed framework jointly controls local shape and mass distortions, while adapting the target domain during the optimization process. It enables three progressively more flexible target-domain settings for the parameterization: a prescribed solid ellipsoid, a volume-normalized adaptive ellipsoid with variable radii, and a sea-embedded free-boundary domain. For each setting, the parameterization algorithm consists of a 3D quasi-conformality shape update, a diffusion-based density-equalizing update, and a geometric correction procedure for removing element foldings, thereby allowing for volumetric parameterizations with different desired effects. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework. Moreover, our framework can be easily applied to multiresolution and localized adaptive volumetric remeshing, volumetric registration, and volumetric morphing. Altogether, our work provides a new way for the representation, processing, and analysis of 3-manifolds.

entries.name: Asymptotic separation of periodic orbits and fractal dimension
entries.abstract: The problem considered in this paper is related to Smale's seventh problem. For a totally bounded metric dynamical system $(X, d, T)$ we introduce a new critical value $\mathfrak s(X, d, T)$ which quantifies the asymptotic separation of periodic orbits. More precisely, $\mathfrak s(X,d,T)$ is defined to be the supremum of all $s\ge 0$ for which there exists a sequence of periodic orbits $\{\mathcal O_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$ in $(X,d,T)$ such that \[ \lim_{k\to \infty} \#\mathcal O_k = +\infty \quad \text{and} \quad \liminf_{k\to\infty}\#\mathcal O_k\cdotη(\mathcal O_k)^s >0, \] where $η(\mathcal O_k)$ denotes the smallest distance between distinct points in $\mathcal O_k$. When the dynamical system is induced by a self-similar iterated function system $\mathcal F$ satisfying the strong separation condition, we prove that this critical value is equal to the Hausdorff dimension $s_{\mathcal F}$ of its self-similar attractor. Furthermore, by using the relative entropy method we show that the associated empirical periodic measures converge weakly to the normalized $s_{\mathcal F}$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on the self-similar attractor.

entries.name: Sectional category versus module sectional category for retractive maps
entries.abstract: We construct a map between simply connected rational spaces of finite rational type which admits a homotopy retraction and satisfies $msecat(p)=2<secat(p)=3$. The target is the rationalization of a simply connected twelve-dimensional CW complex with eleven cells, and is rationally hyperbolic. This disproves Carrasquel--Vera's conjecture for retractive maps.

entries.name: Descartes' rule of signs for polynomial systems
entries.abstract: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We generalize this rule to fewnomial systems with any number of monomials: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes' rules of signs for circuits of Bihan--Dickenstein and Bihan--Dickenstein--Forsgård. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii--Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a chamber $Δ$ of a hyperplane arrangement determined by the coefficients. We bound this number by the Bézout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends with the Descartes' rules for circuits. Restricting the recursion to coherent chambers, in which no cancellation occurs in the facet-count formula, gives weaker bounds in closed form.

entries.name: Cycles and Symmetries of Non-Transitive Dice with Minimal and Uniform Winning Advantages
entries.abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We investigate properties of the directed graphs arising from minimal and uniform winning advantages, including embeddings, isolated vertices and an involutive antiautomorphism. For every \(n\geq9\), we construct a non-transitive triple admitting no pairwise ties with uniform and minimal winning advantage. Moreover, for every \(n\geq7\), we construct a non-transitive triple which is invariant under the involutive antiautomorphism. We consider a two-player game utilizing these constructions and investigate the winning probabilities as \(n\) increases. We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\geq3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage, and identify the two unique such cycles. Finally, we present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is also the largest such \(n\).

entries.name: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
entries.abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

entries.name: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
entries.abstract: Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.

entries.name: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
entries.abstract: We find many exotic connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the split real group $G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call $α$-bundles and $β$-bundles, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold $\mathscr{M}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow \mathsf{G}_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic. These are the first higher rank examples of connected components of a character variety containing multiple (in fact, arbitrarily many) exotic components of Anosov representations.

entries.name: Prevalence of the periodicity of maximizing measures
entries.abstract: For a continuous map $T\colon X\rightarrow X$ on a compact metric space $(X,d)$, we say that a function $f\colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ has the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ if its time averages along forward orbits of $T$ are maximized at a periodic orbit. In this article, we establish the Hunt--Ott conjecture (cf.~\cite{HO96a,HO96b}), that is, the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ is prevalent (in the sense of Hunt--Sauer--Yorke) in the space of Lipschitz functions with respect to a standard metric for subshifts of finite type. This result is a strengthening of \cite[Theorem~A]{BZ16} and \cite[Theorem~1.1]{DLZ24}, confirms the prediction mentioned in the ICM proceeding contribution of Bochi (\cite[Section~1]{Boc18}) suggested by experimental evidence.

entries.name: The truncated $\mathbb{Z}-$moment problem
entries.abstract: We study the truncated moment problem on the one-dimensional full integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, seeking necessary and sufficient conditions for a prescribed sequence of $n$ real numbers to be $\mathbb{Z}-$representable, i.e. to be the sequence of the first $n$ moments of a probability measure supported on $\mathbb{Z}$. Building on the approach developed in 2017 in Infusino et al. for the truncated moment problem on the non-negative integers, we establish a complete characterization of $\mathbb{Z}-$representable sequences for every truncation order $n$. From this result, we derive an inductive and computable $\mathbb{Z}-$representability criterion. More generally, we also investigate the relationship between the truncated $\mathbb{Z}-$moment problem and the truncated Hamburger moment problem, seen as its continuous counterpart.

entries.name: Weitzenbeock's theorem in arbitrary characteristic
entries.abstract: Let \(k\) be a field and \(V\) a finite-dimensional rational representation of the additive group \(\GG_{a,k}\). We show that the ring of invariants \(k[V]^{\GG_a}\) is finitely generated in every characteristic, extending Weitzenböck's classical theorem beyond characteristic zero.

entries.name: On the Convergence of Discrete-Time Primal-Dual Algorithm for Distributed GNE Seeking
entries.abstract: We investigate the convergence of a discrete-time distributed primal-dual algorithm for generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) seeking in a class of noncooperative games with nonlinear coupling constraints. We establish semi-global convergence of the algorithm under a fixed stepsize, in the sense that convergence can be guaranteed from any prescribed compact set of initial conditions by choosing a sufficiently small stepsize. Under a diminishing stepsize sequence, we further establish global convergence when the constraints are globally Lipschitz continuous. For the special case of affine constraints, global convergence is also guaranteed under a sufficiently small fixed stepsize. Finally, we extend these convergence results to a fully distributed GNE seeking algorithm in a partial-decision information setting, where each agent only has access to the actions of its neighbors. These results complement existing convergence results for continuous-time primal-dual dynamics, and provide new convergence guarantees for the discrete-time counterpart in distributed GNE seeking.

entries.name: Time-optimal travel driven by two vector fields on a Riemannian manifold
entries.abstract: We study minimum-time travel on a Riemannian manifold $(M,h)$ for a kinematic model in which finitely many drift fields contribute additively to the velocity, after independent rescaling of their components parallel and orthogonal to a chosen unit direction $u$. The velocity is then $\mathcal Y_x(u)=(η(x)+h_x(\widehat Z_x,u))u+\widehat W_x$, $u\in UT_xM$, for two effective vector fields $\widehat Z$, $\widehat W$ and a self-propulsion speed $η\geq0$. Let $F$ be the gauge of the radial hull $\mathcal B_x=[0,1]\cdot\mathcal S_x$ of the velocity set $\mathcal S_x=\mathcal Y_x(UT_xM)$. Where $η>0$, we characterize when $F$ is a Finsler metric and give two-sided estimates and representation formulae for it; where $η=0$ and $\widehat Z\neq0$, we recover the Randers, Kropina and strong-wind regimes of Zermelo navigation. Examples include Matsumoto's slope metric, traction-modified slope models, and alternative models for wildfire propagation and microswimmer navigation. Since $F$ need not be a Finsler metric, we treat the minimum-time problem with tools from differential inclusions. For distinct endpoints, the inclusions defined by $\mathcal S_x$ and $\mathcal B_x$ give the same infimum travel time, and so does the convex hull of $\mathcal B_x$ under local controllability at the terminal point. When $F$ is finite, the infimum is attained if $(M,h)$ is complete, $\mathcal Y$ is bounded and each $\mathcal B_x$ is convex. When $F$ is a Finsler metric on $\{η>0\}$, the set $\{η=0\}$ cannot be reached from $\{η>0\}$ in finite time and, on $\{η>0\}$, the minimum time is the Finsler distance; if moreover $(M,h)$ is complete and $η$ is bounded, $F$ is forward and backward complete and the minimum time is attained by geodesics. We also compute the support Hamiltonian directly from the velocity law, for every $η\geq0$.

entries.name: The positive-sphere variant of Tingley's problem for $C^1([0,1])$
entries.abstract: Let $C^1([0,1])$ be endowed with the norm $\|f\|=\|f\|_\infty+\|f'\|_\infty$, and let $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ be the part of its unit sphere consisting of nonnegative, nondecreasing functions. We prove that every surjective isometry of $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ is the identity and has a unique surjective real-linear isometric extension to $C^1([0,1])$.

entries.name: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
entries.abstract: We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts. Second, approximate the full evolution operator using a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki (LTS) decomposition of the desired approximation order in time step. The I-LTS construction ensures that the full evolution operator can be represented as a product of terms that each have an efficient explicit tensor product factorization that can be handled efficiently with tensor network and/or quantum block-encoding methods. Next, we apply this method to an important non-integrable point example of a dynamical system: the Stepanoff flow on the torus. First, we derive an efficient unitary quantum algorithm for simulating the Stepanoff flow that can be thought of as a unitary classical version of a quantum map. Then, we provide a detailed description of the encoding of the two-dimensional system into an efficient quantum circuit, including an efficient block-encoding for all required operators. An efficient Hamiltonian simulation algorithm is constructed using a sequence of alternating quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) and Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) circuits. Finally, the circuit is simulated using a numerical emulator of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and the results are found to be consistent with several alternative classical computational methods. While efficient, the need for Trotterization introduces fundamental complexity in requiring small enough time step for an accurate approximation and solving for the transfer operator requires one to confront the linear scaling of the advection operator with grid size.

entries.name: On the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups
entries.abstract: Recall that a class of groups $\mathfrak{F}$ is called $D_\mathfrak{X}$-closed if it contains every group $G = MN$ where $M$ and $N$ are normal $\mathfrak{F}$-subgroups of $G$ and $M\cap N\in \mathfrak{X}$. We prove that a hereditary formation of $ω$-soluble groups is an $n$-multiply $ω$-local formation if and only if it is a $D_{\mathfrak{N}^n_ω}$-closed formation. As corollaries we obtain the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about saturation of hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups and its extension to the class of all $π$-soluble groups, as well as the criterion for a formation of soluble groups to be $n$-multiply local.

entries.name: Zero-cycles and holomorphic forms in families
entries.abstract: We establish parallel Chow and Hodge-theoretic rigidity theorems for dominant projective morphisms between smooth complex varieties. For instance, if the general fiber satisfies $CH_0(F) = \mathbb{Z}$, then the same is true of every fiber. Similarly, if the general fiber is connected with $H^0(F, Ω_F^p) = 0$ for $p > 0$, then the same is true of every fiber. This extends the case of rationally connected fibrations from [Bur26]. We further introduce higher Chow-theoretic notions of singularities.

entries.name: Territorial Conflict as a Cellular Automaton: Frozen Domains and Active Fronts in a Risk-Derived Local Rule
entries.abstract: We formulate the attack and fortification rules of the game Risk as a synchronous cellular automaton on a graph, with battles resolved by exact dice odds. We prove, and verify in Lean, that for the default exchange ratio the rule has radius 6, or 5 for deterministic battles with a positive attack threshold, both attained; that its deterministic form is irreversible except at the highest attack thresholds without growth and with fortification absent or inactive; that without troop growth it freezes in finite time; and that the dynamics near an interface is locally determined. The coupling of the ownership field to a troop field separates frozen domains from active fronts: with a positive attack threshold, saturated domains cannot be conquered, while interfaces with heterogeneous troops keep fighting. In 14252 runs, with attractors classified operationally in Wolfram's scheme, raising the attack threshold takes the system from dominance by one faction to a frozen fragmented partition. The share of the largest faction drops between the same two threshold values at every size up to L=128, in a step about 0.5 wide under a continuous threshold (L=64-96), whereas the probability of complete consolidation is a size-dependent crossover governed by saturated minority domains. Long-period attractors combine spatially fixed local oscillators; apparent class-IV gliders are artefacts of index-ordered tie-breaking. Straight fronts stayed within two cells of their initial position for up to 500,000 steps, over which they are one-dimensional automata with non-recurrent, incompressible dynamics and positive Lyapunov speeds, constant for L>=48. Compared with mean-field and random-regular-graph controls, the lattice lengthens conflicts about twentyfold and clusters conquest: a cell next to a fresh conquest is about five times as likely as average to be conquered next, against 1.1-1.5 in the controls.

entries.name: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
entries.abstract: We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property. By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.

entries.name: The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees
entries.abstract: We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.

entries.name: Monoid Representation of the Determinants of the Adjacency Matrices of 1-joined Path Graphs
entries.abstract: Following previous work by these authors, this paper explores all labeled path graphs joined by 1 edge where the labeling contains the information on how to join that graph. The algebraic structure that this operation has on the determinant of the adjacency matrix of the graph gives a finite monoid of matrices under matrix multiplication. We completely characterize the monoid using the representation theory discussed in Khovanov et al(2024). Finally, we demonstrate how these results can be used to find general formulas for the determinants of chains of 1-joined labeled paths.

entries.name: Discotic columnar phase in a three-dimensional monomer-tetramer model of Heilmann and Lieb with side-to-side attraction
entries.abstract: We study Model III of Heilmann--Lieb (1979), a lattice model for liquid crystals consisting of tetramers (plaquettes) on the cubic lattice at chemical potential $μ$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction of strength $a>0$ between coplanar, aligned tetramers. The model was conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperature provided that $μ+2a>0$. We establish discotic columnar order throughout this regime, fully resolving the conjecture. Specifically, we prove the existence of exactly twelve extremal and periodic Gibbs measures, each breaking rotational symmetry, with one of three tetramer orientations dominant, and translational symmetry in exactly two directions, with one of four tetramer parities dominant within that orientation. Thus, the tetramers form one-dimensional columns arranged on a square lattice. This arrangement is not a priori evident from the zero-temperature picture, where energy only enforces a layered structure: each layer is fully packed and crystalline, but different layers are free to shift independently within their planes. The main novelty here lies in showing how thermal fluctuations lift this degeneracy in favor of the twelve ground states in which all tetramers share a common parity.

entries.name: Cosmological rigidity in $3$ spacetime dimensions
entries.abstract: We establish rigidity theorems for cosmological spacetimes in $3$ spacetime dimensions. In the setting of the Bartnik Splitting Conjecture, under the additional assumptions of null geodesic completeness and the dominant energy condition, we show that the spatial topology is either spherical or the spacetime splits as a product. Our methods rely on the theory of marginally outer trapped surfaces, known rigidity results in the presence of a timelike or null line, and more recent rigidity results in the context of Penrose's singularity theorem due to the first two authors, from which the existence of a foliation by totally geodesic null hypersurfaces can be concluded. Our second main result closes the argument by establishing a splitting theorem for cosmological and null geodesically complete $3$-dimensional spacetimes which satisfy the dominant energy condition and which admit a foliation of the aforementioned type. In its proof, we make use of the local Kundt structure of the metric and construct a global parallel generator for the null foliation.

entries.name: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks
entries.abstract: In order to bound approximation errors for deep neural networks, we split the problem into two steps: First the selection of optimal infinite width limits for each layer and second an optimal discretization of all layers to obtain finite sized networks. We show that in expectation, the latter problem is equivalently characterized by a layer wise generalization of Barron norms. Moreover, we provide an analysis of the optimization landscape and show that local minima are characterized by an equidistribution principle akin to similar ideas in adaptive spline and finite element approximation.

entries.name: Linearization of completely Lipschitz functions
entries.abstract: We develop a linearization theory for completely Lipschitz mappings between operator spaces. Motivated by the classical theory of Lipschitz-free spaces, we introduce a completely Lipschitz-free space and show that completely Lipschitz mappings admit a canonical linearization as completely bounded operators on this space. We provide several equivalent descriptions of this operator space, extending to the noncommutative setting the classical constructions of Arens--Eells, de Leeuw, and Dixmier--Ng. In particular, we obtain a molecular description, a quotient representation of an operator $\ell_1$-space, and a realization as the closed linear span of evaluation functionals. Our framework applies over both the real and complex scalar fields; in the real case, we first establish some operator space results needed to carry out the constructions. We also show that our notion of completely Lipschitz mapping encompasses the previously introduced extensions of Lipschitz mappings to operator spaces. These results provide a unified framework for studying Lipschitz phenomena in the setting of operator spaces and establish the corresponding free operator spaces as a natural tool for their linearization.

entries.name: PrO Filtering via Kernel Mean Embedding Dynamics
entries.abstract: Filtering methods are routinely deployed with misspecified state-space models, where Bayesian filters can diverge and become overconfident. Predictively-oriented (PrO) filtering is a recent, hyperparameter-free alternative that was demonstrated to outperform (generalised) Bayesian filtering methods when either the dynamical model or the measurement model is structurally misspecified. This can be attributed to \emph{hedging} behaviour: when an observation conflicts with the forecast, the PrO update places mass near both. Yet existing implementations of PrO filtering rely on unimodal (Gaussian) approximations, whose ability to effectively hedge is limited. This paper develops the first nonparametric, particle-based implementation of PrO filtering. The key obstacle, that PrO filtering distributions are only implicitly defined, is overcome by constructing a path from the predictive to the PrO filtering distribution whose rate is available in closed form, enabling the use of kernel mean embedding dynamics for measure transport. The resulting algorithm requires only simulation from the dynamical model and evaluations of the likelihood, with neither importance weights nor the predictive density. Moreover, as we prove, the number of pseudo-time steps it requires does not grow with the outlyingness of the observation, in contrast to transport along the Bayesian tempering path. An empirical assessment shows substantial improvement over Gaussian variation of PrO filtering in challenging nonlinear examples where Gaussian approximation is unreasonably limited.

entries.name: Supercritical Nodal Solutions on Annuli: Symmetry Breaking and Multiplicity
entries.abstract: We establish existence and multiplicity results for nonradial sign-changing solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu=a(|x|)|u|^{p-2}u$ on annuli in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\geq4$, $a$ is a positive radial coefficient, and $p$ may exceed the Sobolev critical exponent. For each decomposition $N=m+n$, with $m\geq n\geq2$, we minimize the energy on a nodal Nehari set within a signed cone of angularly nondecreasing, $O(m)\times O(n)$-invariant functions. Whenever $2<p<2(m+1)/(m-1)$, the minimum is attained, and every minimizer is a classical solution with exactly two nodal domains. A cone-preserving auxiliary Dirichlet operator and a two-parameter energy deformation recover the full equation from the constrained minimization. We prove that these minimizers are nonradial if $(p-2)β_Ω>2N$, where $β_Ω$ is the optimal Dirichlet Hardy constant associated with the weight $|x|^{-2}$. Under a common admissible exponent range satisfying this condition, different orthogonal decompositions yield distinct solution pairs $\{\pm u\}$. An explicit lower bound for $β_Ω$ provides supercritical regimes on sufficiently thin annuli in which the nonradiality and multiplicity results apply.

entries.name: A Rellich-type inequality for the sphere
entries.abstract: We prove a Rellich-type inequality of the form $$\int |(Δ+ 1)u|^2dx \geq C_d \int \frac{|u|^2}{(1 - |x|^2)^2}dx $$ for smooth functions $u$ compactly supported in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 1$. The obtained constant is asymptotically sharp up to the first three orders, as $d \rightarrow \infty$. We also show that in the complement of the ball, the inequality holds only in dimension one, and does not hold true with a positive $C_d>0$ for $d \geq 2$. The motivation is that if $\hat{u}$ denotes the Fourier transform of $u$, then the inequality is associated with the uncertainty principle $$ \left(\int |u|^2dx\right)^2 \lesssim \int (1-|x|^2)^2|u|^2dx \int (1 - |ξ|^2)^2|\hat{u}|^2 dξ,$$ which says that a function cannot be simultaneously concentrated on a sphere in both space and frequency. This is in analogy with the classical Hardy inequality together with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

entries.name: Oleinik estimate for a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit
entries.abstract: In this article, we establish an Oleinik type estimate for $2\times2$ systems of hyperbolic conservation laws in a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit. More precisely, we consider the parabolic approximation with vanishing viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon u_{xx}$ ($\varepsilon>0$) for the Temple class of hyperbolic system of conservation laws and for these approximate solutions we obtain an Oleinik type estimate uniformly with respect to the viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon>0$. This extends the Oleinik inequality for scalar conservation laws with viscosity to the system. Subsequently, we prove that these approximate solutions converge via the process of vanishing viscosity limit to a global weak solution of the limit strictly hyperbolic system provided that the initial data is small in $L^\infty$. To do this we implement the vanishing viscosity method of Bianchini and Bressan [Indiana Univ. Math. J. 2000] with $L^\infty$ initial data which requires new tools as an local in time Oleinik estimate (obtained by employing a suitable maximum principle and a normal form argument) and a localization argument. In particular we need to introduce appropriate weight functions which satisfy a Bellman equation to get new localized transversal interaction estimates.

entries.name: Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
entries.abstract: Linearized Reed-Solomon codes (LRS) are optimal sum-rank-metric codes that generalize both Reed-Solomon and Gabidulin codes, and benefit from excellent decoding capabilities, making them potentially interesting candidates for post-quantum code-based cryptography. Previous works have investigated the underlying geometric structure of LRS codes, identifying geometric invariants that distinguish them from random codes. Other works have proposed approaches to recovering the LRS structure from an arbitrary generator matrix, together with additional data. However, both the distinguishers and the recovery techniques proposed so far are either not fully general, or have a prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time procedure for the full structure recovery of LRS codes from the sole knowledge of an arbitrary generator matrix. Our results show that, like their Hamming and rank metric counterparts, LRS codes cannot be used as they are for McEliece-like encryption. Our approach combines Overbeck-type attacks with suitable matrix manipulations and shortening techniques to recover the evaluation parameters across different ranges of code dimensions.

entries.name: The Vinogradov system in finite fields and two-source extractors with arbitrarily small min-entropy rate
entries.abstract: Fix $k\ge2$ and $1/(k+1)<ρ\le1$. Let $q=p^n$, where the prime $p$ is fixed and sufficiently large in terms of $k,ρ$, and $n$ tends to infinity through prime values. We show that for every $A\subseteq\F_q$ with $|A|\ge q^ρ$, the Vinogradov system of degree $k$ in $2s$ variables has at most $|A|^{2s}q^{-k/2-η}$ solutions in $A$. Here the integer $s$ and the saving $η>0$ depend only on $k,ρ,p$. At $ρ=1/(k+1)$ an example rules out every saving $η>0$ in this moment estimate. For $k=2$ the author previously proved the analogous estimate over prime fields. We deduce a power saving for the double sums of $e(xy+(xy)^2+\dots+(xy)^k)$ over any two sets of size at least $q^ρ$, where $e$ is any nontrivial additive character of $\F_q$. Choosing $k$ sufficiently large gives a polynomial two-source extractor with exponentially small error at every fixed positive min-entropy rate. The proof of the moment estimate uses the theorem of Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao on Marton's conjecture and a bound for the intersection of the moment curve with an affine subspace over $\F_p$.

entries.name: A non-Morse relatively Anosov group
entries.abstract: We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.

entries.name: Quot schemes on projective space
entries.abstract: We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We show that the radius of Hilbert and Quot schemes can grow linearly with the dimension of the subschemes being parametrized, and construct the first examples of Hilbert schemes of curves with radius two. For absolutely split bundles on projective space, we construct a distinguished generically smooth component and classify all smooth Quot schemes. In most cases, we give explicit geometric descriptions in terms of products of generalized flag varieties and projective bundles over Grassmannians.

entries.name: Miyazawa invariants of satellite surfaces
entries.abstract: We prove formulas describing the behavior of Miyazawa's degree invariant of knotted spheres and real projective planes in the 4-sphere under satellite operations. As an application, we show that every deform-spun real projective plane admits infinitely many topologically but not smoothly isotopic copies. In particular, we produce an infinite exotic family of irreducible real projective planes containing Hughes-Kim-Miller-Nahm's counterexample to the Kinoshita conjecture.

entries.name: Well-foundedness of the strict Lipschitz order on countably complete filters
entries.abstract: In $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{DC}$, the strict Lipschitz order on proper countably complete filters on any fixed ordinal is well-founded. The proof uses transfinite recursion and closure under countable intersections to derive a contradiction from a descending chain. Restricting each filter to the least ordinal it contains yields a set-like well-founded order that compares filters on different ordinals. In $\mathsf{ZF}$, two ultrafilters on the same ordinal are equal if each is nonexpansively reducible to the other. These results answer both parts of Question 9.2.11 in The Ultrapower Axiom.

entries.name: On Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks
entries.abstract: We study Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Szép products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Szép factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Szép actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.

entries.name: Real equiangular lines in dimensions 18-20 and sharp fixed-angle bounds
entries.abstract: In collaboration with OpenAI's GPT-6, we prove that the maximum numbers of real equiangular lines in dimensions 18, 19, and 20 are $N(18)=57$, $N(19)=72$, and $N(20)=90$, respectively. We reduce the upper bounds to paired lattice points in sections of even unimodular lattices of rank twenty-four. Root-system estimates, exact certificates, and Golay-code arguments bound the sections. In the Leech lattice, generalized Hamming weights of a binary evaluation code give sharp bounds attained by nested sections. At prescribed cosine $1/q$, we also show that $N_{1/q}(d)=d+7$ for explicit intervals of consecutive dimensions for each odd $q\ge319$, and $N_{1/q}(d)=d+23$ on such intervals for each odd $q\ge5599$. Regular graphs in repeated Seidel blocks vary the cosine while preserving nullity, and a coherence bound proves optimality. Symmetric conference matrices give a further sharp family at quadratic irrational cosines.

entries.name: Adaptive Control Barrier Functions for Nonlinear Singularly Perturbed Systems
entries.abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) have emerged as a flexible and efficient approach for enforcing dynamic safety constraints. In this paper, we consider a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with singular perturbations and develop an adaptive CBF framework for such systems to enforce safety constraints on both the slow and fast subsystems in the overall singularly perturbed nonlinear system with uncertain parameters. We first develop a robustness property showing that if an adaptive controller for the slow subsystem satisfies the slow CBF condition with an appropriate safety margin, then for sufficiently small values of the singular perturbation parameter $\varepsilon$, the slow subsystem remains within an $O(\varepsilon)$-neighborhood of its safe set. We then consider the more general case of safety constraints on both the fast and slow subsystems and provide conditions under which joint slow-fast safety is achieved despite the parametric uncertainties. The reduced-order slow model and the slow and fast CBF conditions are evaluated using an online parameter estimate and the parameter mismatch between the estimated and true reduced-order models is addressed via a state-dependent robustness margin in the CBF inequalities. To illustrate the proposed framework, we present simulation studies for two systems with parametric uncertainties: a synthetic two-time-scale fourth-order example system and a unicycle with a fast turn-rate actuator and an obstacle avoidance safety constraint.

entries.name: Exponential integrability of SLE Minkowski content
entries.abstract: Let $0<κ<8$, $d=1+κ/8$, and $q=2/(2-d)$. Let $μ$ be the $d$-dimensional Minkowski content measure of either chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ in $\mathbb H$ from $0$ to $\infty$ or two-sided whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ through $0$. We prove that there exist constants $c_κ,C_κ\in(0,\infty)$ such that \[ \mathbb E\exp\left\{c_κ\left(\frac{μ(D)}{(\operatorname{diam} D)^d}\right)^q\right\}\le C_κ\] for every deterministic bounded Borel set $D$ of positive diameter in the corresponding domain. The exponent $q$ in this moment bound is optimal in both settings. We also show that, almost surely, $μ(B(z,r))=O\bigl(r^d(\log(1/r))^{1/q}\bigr)$ as $r\downarrow0$, locally uniformly in $z$.

entries.name: Extensions of congruent monotileable (and amenable) groups
entries.abstract: A monotile of a countable group $G$ is a finite subset $F \subseteq G$ that tiles $G$, namely $G=\bigsqcup_{c\in C} c F$, for some set of centers $C\subseteq G$. The group $G$ is called congruent monotileable (CM) if it admits an exhaustive sequence of monotiles $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that each $F_{n+1}$ is teselated by $F_n$. If moreover $G$ is amenable and the sequence $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is Folner, we say $G$ is congruent monotileable amenable (CMA). In this work we observe that the classes of CM and CMA groups are stable under group extensions satisfying a certain technical condition, which we call $stepwise$ $monotileability$, and which is a weaker version of the notion of $X$-$monotileability$ introduced by Dikranjan $et al$. Our condition also includes central extensions previously considered by Gao, Jackson, Seward for CM groups, and by Cecchi Bernales, Cortez for CMA groups. We show that this condition is satisfied by semidirect products of the form $G\wr H$, provided $G$ and $H$ are CM/CMA groups, and also by extensions of locally finite groups by CM/CMA groups. This furnishes new examples of CM and CMA groups. In particular, we provide the first examples of finitely generated CMA groups which are neither solvable nor residually finite.

entries.name: Strong Ill-Posedness for the Surface Quasi-Geostrophic Equations in $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$
entries.abstract: We establish ill-posedness of the surface quasi-geostrophic equations in Sobolev spaces $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every integer $k \geq 3$. This includes the scaling critical space $W^{3,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We build on ideas from (arXiv:2610.04872); in particular, we use a theorem of Bonami and Poornima to construct a basic building block, or packet, which obeys a linear evolution approximating that of the perturbation of the background solution to SQG. The Bonami-Poornima theorem ensures that this packet has both small initial $W^{k,1}$ norm and large $W^{k,1}$ norm at positive times. We then implement a process known as many packet dilution, which allows one to construct an initial perturbation as a sum of sufficiently many packets to dilute the effect of the nonlinear term. This initial perturbation leads to the desired norm inflation. To establish instantaneous blow-up of the $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ norm, we also prove a local well-posedness result in the critical Sobolev-Lorentz space $W^{2,(2,1)}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. This result gives a uniform lower bound on the existence time for solutions with bounded $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ data, even though the solutions' $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms may become arbitrarily large in arbitrarily short time.

entries.name: Weakly Pointed Fusion $Π$-supercategories over fields of characteristic not two
entries.abstract: We study a class of weakly pointed fusion $Π$-supercategories over a field $k$ of characteristic not equal to $2$, with unit $\mathbf 1$ satisfying $\mathrm{End}(\mathbf 1) = k$. Assuming the existence of a Brauer--Wall reference category over $k$, we classify these categories up to monoidal equivalence. We show that Brauer--Wall reference categories exist for $k = \mathbb C, \mathbb R$ but not for $k = \mathbb F_5$. For each finite group $G$, we also study a product of these categories equipped with a $G$-grading and define a group $\mathcal T_k(G)$, giving an explicit formula for the multiplication in terms of group cochains for $k = \mathbb C$ and $\mathbb R$.

entries.name: Asymptotic isoperimetry for parallelohedra
entries.abstract: The smallest possible surface area of a convex translational tile of $\mathbb R^n$ approaches $\sqrt{2}$ times that of a ball of equal volume as $n\to\infty$. For the lower bound, we combine Gaussian smoothing with the Milman-Neeman multi-bubble theorem. For the upper bound, we use Siegel mean value theorem to average over lattice Voronoi cells. Our method also yields convex $\mathbb Z^n$-tiles whose orthogonal projection onto any hyperplane has volume $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, answering a question of Naor and Regev.

entries.name: Pairing Powers of Pythagorean Pairs II
entries.abstract: Let $(a,b,c)$ be a pythagorean triple, i.e., $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Then $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$ are hypotenuse-leg pairs (hl-pairs), i.e., pairs $(c,d)$ of positive integers such that $c^2-d^2$ is a non-zero square. An hl-pair $(c,d)$ is called a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if there is a pythagorean pair $(k,l)$, which is not a multiple of the pythagorean pair $(d,\sqrt{c^2-d^2})$, such that $(c^hk,d^hl)$ is again an hl-pair. To each hl-pair $(c,d)$ and each $h\geq 1$ we assign the elliptic curve $Γ_{c^h,d^h}: y^2=x^3+(c^{2h}-d^{2h})x^2-c^{2h}d^{2h}x$ and show that its torsion group is $\Bbb Z/2\Bbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ and that $(c,d)$ is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if and only if $Γ_{c^h,d^h}$ has positive rank over $\mathbb Q$. In this case there are infinitely many such pythagorean pairs $(k,l)$, not multiples of each other. Moreover, every hl-pair is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $1$ and a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $3$, and we give sufficient conditions for degree $2$. The two cases $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$, where $a=m^2-n^2$ and $b=2mn$, are worked out separately.

entries.name: Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching
entries.abstract: A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs. We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last $m$ observations to the nearest regime mean. For two regimes with conditionally independent, stochastically ordered observations, a switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly $1/2$. Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most $\bar P(m)+\bar s(m-1)/2$, where $\bar P(m)$ is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and $\bar s$ the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly $1/2$, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor $p_{\min}^{m-1}$. For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of $σ^2/Δ^2$, depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is $\bar s\log(1/\bar s)/(2I)(1+o(1))$, with $I$ the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most $2\log2\approx1.39$, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with $\pm1$ steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.

entries.name: Unbounded DiPerna-Lions commutators for Osgood-Sobolev vector fields
entries.abstract: In this paper we show that there exists a regime of Osgood-Sobolev vector fields in which the DiPerna-Lions scheme cannot be applied despite the recently proved well-posedness and propagation of regularity in arXiv:2607.28118. For Osgood-Sobolev vector fields we also show that the propagation of regularity proved in arXiv:2607.28118 is sharp and derive lower bounds on mixing.

entries.name: On the Distribution of Prime Factors of $\lfloor αn^2 \rfloor$
entries.abstract: Let $α> 0$ be irrational. We show that $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ obeys a Gaussian distribution. That is, for $n$ chosen uniformly at random from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, the random variable $(ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to the standard Gaussian as $N$ tends to infinity. Additionally, we fully describe the distribution of $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ for a positive rational $α$.

entries.name: Sums of Kloosterman fractions and applications
entries.abstract: We obtain improved bounds for bilinear and trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions, building on the works of Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec and Bettin-Chandee. Our results use the spectral theory of automorphic forms, and save $N^{1/12} A^{1/3}$ over the trivial bound when $M = N$ and $A$ is small. In the exceptional Maass spectrum, we rely on a new large sieve inequality with averaging over the levels, which may be of independent interest. Applications include an asymptotic for the second moment of the zeta function twisted by a Dirichlet polynomial of length $T^{0.532}$ (improving Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill's $T^{0.515}$ and Dong-Robles-Zeindler's $T^{0.518}$), as well as an improved level of distribution for unbalanced convolutions (improving results of Fouvry-Radziwill, Wright, and Dong-Robles-Zeindler).

entries.name: Monoidal analog of cluster-tilting theory and monoidal reachability of acyclic cluster algebras
entries.abstract: In this paper, we prove that many analogous facts of cluster-tilting theory holds in monoidal categories from quantum affine algebras or quiver Hecke algebras. We show that a maximal commuting family of real prime modules, which is an analogous object of a cluster-tilting object, is always a laurent family introduced by Kashiwara-Kim-Oh-Park. By using $\widetildeΛ$-invariants, we construct an exchange matrix of each laurent family and show that a laurent family is always completely $Λ$-admissible monoidal seed. We obtain that a pair of real prime modules is an exchange pair if and only if $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is $1$. When the category is a monoidal categorification of a cluster algebra of acyclic type, we prove that $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is not less than generic Ext invariant by using tropical $F$-invariant introduced by Cao and Fei. Moreover, we show that, the conjecture asserting that real simple modules correspond exactly to cluster monomials holds in these cases.

entries.name: Invariance of log plurigenera in families of compact Kähler manifolds
entries.abstract: Let $(X_t,B_t)$ be a smooth proper family of pairs with Kähler fibres, where the boundary has relative simple normal crossings and real coefficients in $[0,1)$. We show that for every $m\ge1$, every section of $mK_{X_t}+\lfloor mB_t\rfloor$ extends locally over the base. In particular, the log plurigenera are locally constant, and for $B_t=0$ we obtain the deformation invariance of the plurigenera $P_m(X_t)$. Since the total space need not be Kähler, we run the minimal model program on the central fibre, using the work of Hacon-Wang and Hacon-Xie, and extend its steps over a disc. The obstruction to lifting a jet vanishes along the fixed part determined by the final model, and so it is square-integrable for the weight in the extension theorem of Cao-Păun. As an application, if the adjoint is pseudoeffective on one fibre, then the pair has a relative good minimal model near each point of the base and a relative canonical model over the whole base.

entries.name: The Riemann hypothesis
entries.abstract: The Weyl symbolic calculus of operators leads to the construction, if one takes for symbol a certain distribution decomposing over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, of an operator with the following property: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the validity of a collection of estimates involving this operator. Pseudodifferential arithmetic, a novel chapter of pseudodifferential operator theory, makes it possible to make the operator under study fully explicit. This leads to a proof of the conjecture.

entries.name: Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II
entries.abstract: In this article, we prove several transfer principles for the cohomological dimension of fields. Given a fixed field $K$ with finite cohomological dimension $δ$, the two main ones allow to: - construct totally ramified extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq δ- 1$ when $K$ is a complete discrete valuation field; - construct algebraic extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq δ-1$ and satisfying a norm condition. We then apply these results to Serre's conjecture II and to some variants for fields of any cohomological dimension that are inspired by conjectures of Kato and Kuzumaki. In particular, we prove that Serre's conjecture II for characteristic $0$ fields implies Serre's conjecture II for positive characteristic fields.

entries.name: Algebraic cycles on some Fano varieties. Part I: Quartic double fivefolds
entries.abstract: We study algebraic cycles on quartic double fivefolds, which are Fano fivefolds whose middle cohomology is numerically similar to that of a Calabi-Yau threefold, continuing the work of Skauli on lines, $1$-cycles and the coniveau filtration on double covers of projective space. By means of cubic surfaces which are totally ramified along the branch locus, we prove the integral Hodge conjecture for all of them. We also show that the comparison maps between their Chow groups and étale Chow groups are isomorphisms except possibly in codimension three, where we describe the kernel and the cokernel in terms of Bloch-Ogus cohomology and, via a Sarkisov link, of the unramified cohomology of a cubic surface over the function field of $\mathbb{P}^3$.

entries.name: Local square mean in the hyperbolic circle problem and sums of Salié sums
entries.abstract: Let $Γ\subseteq \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a finite volume Fuchsian group. The hyperbolic circle problem is the estimation of the number of elements of the $Γ$-orbit of $z$ in a hyperbolic circle around $w$ of radius $R$, where $z$ and $w$ are given points of the upper half plane and $R$ is a large number. An estimate with error term $e^{\frac 23R}$ is known. Recently, taking $z=w$ and considering $Γ= \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, we have shown the estimate $e^{\left(\frac 9{14}+ε\right)R}$ for the local $L^2$-norm of the error term, which is better than the pointwise bound. Here we improve the exponent $\frac 9{14}$, conditionally on a twisted Linnik-Selberg-type conjecture for sums of Salié sums.

entries.name: Equal probabilities maximize the expected deficit in the siblings of the coupon collector
entries.abstract: In the siblings (or brotherhood) variant of the coupon collector's problem, a main collector draws coupons until her own album is complete and passes every duplicate down a chain of siblings; the $j$th collector is then left with $U_j^N$ empty places, $j\ge 2$. It has been conjectured [stated as an open problem in the work that introduced the model] that, for every fixed number of coupon types $N$ and every $j\ge 2$, the expected deficit $\E[U_j^N]$ is maximized by the equiprobable coupon distribution. We prove this in a sharp, finite-$N$ form: $\E[U_j^N]$ is strictly larger at the uniform vector than at any other probability vector, and indeed strictly increases along every ray running from an arbitrary distribution toward the uniform one. The proof is exact and elementary in its ingredients. An inclusion--exclusion step turns the governing Poissonized integral into a one-dimensional integral with a separable integrand; a single integration by parts then rewrites the radial derivative of $\E[U_j^N]$ as a positively weighted covariance of an increasing function, whose sign is settled by Chebyshev's correlation inequality. We show that $\E[U_j^N]$ is \emph{not} Schur-concave, so that no majorization or pairwise-smoothing argument can yield the result, and we explain why the recent variance-extremality method of Long~[Long, arXiv:2604.25108, 2026] does not transfer. As by-products we obtain a finite closed form for $\E[U_j^N]$ over subsets of the coupon set and the exact Hessian of $\E[U_j^N]$ at the uniform vector. The argument extends without change to all real $j>1$.

entries.name: On the First Derivative Bounds for Rational Bézier Curves
entries.abstract: We derive a new upper bound for the first derivative of a rational Bézier curve of degree $n$. The estimate applies to arbitrary degrees and provides a framework for studying the linear bound conjectured by Li et al., whose coefficient is the maximal adjacent weight ratio $Ω$. Within this framework, the conjectured bounds for $n=5$ and $n=6$ are established as special cases, completing the verification for all $n\le6$. The endpoint estimates follow from the classical derivative formulas. For interior parameters, the analysis reduces to a variance-like optimization problem over a compact box of adjacent weight ratios. A block argument reduces the maximization to vertices and one-dimensional faces, leading to a finite family of polynomial inequalities. We further prove that sufficiently fine subdivision yields subcurves satisfying the conjectured estimate with their own weights, control points and local parameters. After parameter rescaling, these local estimates provide a bound for the derivative of the original curve. Numerical examples illustrate the new bound and the subdivision-based estimates and compare them with an existing method.

entries.name: Algebraic Transfer of Gaussian Chaoses: Moment Geometry and Spectral Ideals
entries.abstract: We prove the partition moment conjecture of Adamczak, Latała and Meller for decoupled Gaussian chaoses of every order with coefficients in arbitrary real Banach spaces. The corresponding pairing bound retains partition weights only on the unpaired slots. We give Talagrand's requested construction of admissible partitions for unions of operator ellipsoids and refute Bednorz and Martynek's Bernoulli increment comparison conjecture. For directed operator contractions, we obtain constant-one Schatten bounds and the optimal logarithmic loss for weak Schatten links. Strictly entrywise-positive block matrices refute Li and Zhao's trace-norm compression conjecture. For radial singular Wick multipliers on groups of polynomial growth, we determine exact Schatten thresholds, almost-sure singular-value decay and critical Weyl constants. The constants come from Gaussian Wick matrices in the virtually abelian case and powers of a free circular element otherwise. For finite-group convolutions, we classify projected Plancherel limits and give singular-value and Gaussian eigenvalue limits at general coefficient covariance.

entries.name: Partial $F$-invariants and cluster categorifications
entries.abstract: The $F$-invariant in cluster algebras is a combinatorial invariant that unifies the $E$-invariant from additive categorification and the $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant from monoidal categorification. In this paper, we study its refinement, the partial $F$-invariant, and establish its mutation formula under changes of the initial seed. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Reading, which asserts that the non-compatible cluster variables can be separated by sign-coherence of $g$-vectors upon varying the initial seed. We further show that, for cluster monomials, the partial $F$-invariants coincide with both the partial $E$-invariants for reachable decorated representations of quivers with potentials and the pole orders of normalized $R$-matrices (or partial $\mathfrak{d}$-invariants) for finite-dimensional reachable simple modules over quantum affine algebras. As consequences, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the pole orders for reachable simple modules in terms of $q$-characters; we verify the conjectural explicit formula for the pole orders between Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules.

entries.name: Multiple Zeta Values in Positive Characteristic: A Kaneko-Zagier-Type Conjecture
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study a comparison between $\infty$-adic and finite multiple zeta values in positive characteristic. We construct a surjective comparison map from the algebra of $\infty$-adic multiple zeta values to a quotient of the algebra of finite multiple zeta values. This map factors through the quotient by $ζ_A(q-1)$, thereby establishing the well-definedness of a Kaneko-Zagier-type conjectural map. We further show that the comparison map is compatible with special values of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, as well as with the corresponding $\star$-inverse values. As an application, we prove the upper bound predicted by Shi's dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values.

entries.name: Sectional category versus module sectional category for retractive maps
entries.abstract: We construct a map between simply connected rational spaces of finite rational type which admits a homotopy retraction and satisfies $msecat(p)=2<secat(p)=3$. The target is the rationalization of a simply connected twelve-dimensional CW complex with eleven cells, and is rationally hyperbolic. This disproves Carrasquel--Vera's conjecture for retractive maps.

entries.name: Graded Structures of $v$-adic Carlitz Multiple Polylogarithms and $v$-adic Multiple Zeta Values
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms and $v$-adic multiple zeta values. We prove that, for every finite place $v$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$, the natural weight gives a graded structure on the algebras generated by these values. Moreover, we show that every $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}$-linear relation among these values arises from an $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear relation. In particular, our results establish a function field analogue of the Furusho-Yamashita direct sum conjecture and extend Chen's work from finite places of degree one to arbitrary finite places.

entries.name: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-graphs
entries.abstract: A $3$-graph (meaning a $3$-uniform hypergraph) $H$ is iteratively $3$-partite if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of some lexicographic power of a single hyperedge. We prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu, that for a $3$-graph $H$, the off-diagonal Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is iteratively $3$-partite. As an immediate corollary, we also obtain a resolution of a 2009 problem of Bohman, Frieze and Mubayi, asking for a characterization of all $3$-graphs $H$ for which the minimum number of hyperedges in an $H$-free $3$-graph with chromatic number greater than $k$ is $k^{3+o(1)}$ as $k\to\infty$. We prove a $3$-graph $H$ has the latter property if and only if $H$ is not iteratively $3$-partite.

entries.name: Cycles and Symmetries of Non-Transitive Dice with Minimal and Uniform Winning Advantages
entries.abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We investigate properties of the directed graphs arising from minimal and uniform winning advantages, including embeddings, isolated vertices and an involutive antiautomorphism. For every \(n\geq9\), we construct a non-transitive triple admitting no pairwise ties with uniform and minimal winning advantage. Moreover, for every \(n\geq7\), we construct a non-transitive triple which is invariant under the involutive antiautomorphism. We consider a two-player game utilizing these constructions and investigate the winning probabilities as \(n\) increases. We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\geq3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage, and identify the two unique such cycles. Finally, we present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is also the largest such \(n\).

entries.name: A linear edge bound for k-quasi-planar graphs
entries.abstract: We prove the $k$-quasi-planar graph conjecture for topological drawings. For every integer $k\ge 2$, a simple graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices admitting a drawing with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $1056(k-1)^2(n-2)$ edges. Thus the number of edges is linear in $n$, with an explicit quadratic dependence on $k$. The result allows multiple crossings between the same pair of edges, including edges with a common endpoint. The proof uses the double of a sphere with boundary to represent graph edges by closed geodesics on a hyperbolic surface. The endpoints of geodesic lifts induce partial orders of width at most $k-1$. A stability bound for greedy chain partitions, together with a counting argument over a triangulation, gives the stated edge bound.

entries.name: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
entries.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $Π$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.

entries.name: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
entries.abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojević--Grujić--Živaljević conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.

entries.name: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential
entries.abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

entries.name: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
